main_text.p: est principium cancri: punctum extremum versus meridiem, appellatur solstitium hibernum, quod est principium capricorni. Distantia inter aequatorem & alterutrum horum punctorum, variat pro ratione declinationis eclipticæ ab aequatore: arcus enim ille ex obseruatione sapientis Ptolemæi comprehendit viginti tres gradus, & quinquaginta vnum minuta, quatenus totus circulus diuiditur in 360 partes: sed iuxta Almamonem, & alios, qui eum secuti sunt, sapientes, continet viginti tres gradus, & triginta quinque minuta. [Quomodo autem singulis seculis obseruanda sit summa solis declinatio, in quodam peculia-ri tractatu, si Deus voluerit, ostendam.] Iam ergo patet, planetas motu suo proprio reuolui super polis zodiaci, ab occasu in ortum: voluit autem eos cum reliquis stellis primum mobile, ab oriente in occidentem progrediens. Poli autem æquatoris, circa quos primus motus conspicitur, sunt fixi, neque mouentur: sed poli zodiaci ex motu primo circa polos æquatoris mouentur, quamuis inseparabiles sint ab illo circulo, qui transit polos æquatoris & zodiaci, in quo reperitur motus primus & declinationis.

1 Recte asserit Alfraganus, non manere omnibus seculis vnam & eandem solis declinationem: vnde sequitur etiam anni quantitatem variare pro diuersa temporum ratione. Tempore Ptolemæi summa solis declinatio fuit 23 gradus & 51 minut. seculo Alma-

page.notes: The text is set in one column with the bracketed passage printed in the same paragraph. A stray mark (apostrophe) stands before "Distantia" and is left out. The catchword "monis" completes the hyphenated "Alma-" and is not repeated in the text. Doubtful readings: "reuolui" (the i may carry an accent mark), and "51" in the second paragraph, printed with a figure resembling a long s. The printed "s" and "f" forms are normalised to plain s where they are long s; "s" in the transcription is retained only where the scan shows an actual long s, per the rules, so the output uses plain s throughout.
